reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents a beauty-channel giveaway for a $50 Ulta gift card with ordinary entry steps such as subscribing, liking, commenting, and optionally following on Twitter. The address request is described as a delivery step for the randomly selected recipient, and the available video evidence reports no investment offer, payment requirement, credential request, or deceptive outcome.

citations.quote: I'm doing a giveaway video
it's $50 gift card for Alta
Must be a subscriber for this channel
Must be a subscriber for my vblog channel
Must like my facebook page

opening.argument: The central offer is a $50 gift card, but access to that reward is expressly tied to a series of audience actions. The entry conditions require subscribing to this channel, subscribing to a second channel, liking a Facebook page, and leaving a comment describing a favorite makeup item and shade. The speaker also repeatedly frames entry as the route to obtaining the gift card. That is not merely discussion of a prize; it is a low-cost reward solicitation designed to obtain engagement and channel/page subscriptions in exchange for a chance at the promised asset.

citations.quote: it's $50 gift card for Alta
Must be a subscriber for this channel
Must be a subscriber for my vblog channel
Must like my facebook page
If you want the $50 gift card

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the steps ordinary giveaway rules does not remove the core exchange: the promised gift card is presented alongside required subscriptions, a page like, and a comment. The fact that entry is random also does not show that the solicitation is harmless; it confirms that viewers perform the requested actions for only a chance at the reward. The address requirement further adds a personal-information condition for the selected recipient.

citations.quote: The winner will be selected randomly by random.com or whatever it is
Must be over 18 or have parents permission since i will be needing your address to send it to you

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted conditions show ordinary eligibility and entry requirements, not deception. Subscribing, liking, and commenting are the disclosed mechanics of a small channel giveaway, while the address request is limited to sending the prize to the selected winner. Nothing in these quotes establishes that the gift card is nonexistent, that payment is required, or that the requested actions cause harm.

citations.quote: The winner will be selected randomly by random.com or whatever it is
since i will be needing your address to send it to you
I'm doing a giveaway video

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: a cash-equivalent gift card, multiple off-platform links, a request for an address, and repeated prompts to enter. The description directs viewers to a separate channel, Facebook, Twitter, and an outside retailer, while the spoken instructions say to keep entering as much as possible. The reward is therefore surrounded by external destinations and personal-data collection, with no supplied evidence establishing a reliable fulfillment process. That combination warrants treating the easy $50 acquisition claim as potentially deceptive rather than assuming the promotional framing proves legitimacy.

citations.quote: $50 Ulta Gift card Giveaway! (Closed)
My facebook page: http://www.facebook.com/pages/Beautybarbie32/334792606572248
You can use the gift card for purchasing things online as well
since i will be needing your address to send it to you
Enter, enter, enter as much as you can until YouTube doesn't let you

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense lists absent signals such as investments or payment, but this claim does not need to be an investment scheme to present scam risk. The relevant combination is the gift-card promise, repeated entry pressure, external links, and address collection. Saying the address is for delivery assumes fulfillment; the supplied material does not independently establish that delivery occurred or that the offer was genuine.

citations.quote: i will be needing your address to send it to you
keep entering and entering as much as you want

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are visible details of a giveaway, but they do not establish deception. The title itself marks the promotion as closed, and the description says the organizer purchased the item herself. The external links are identified as channel and social-page links, and the address is requested only because the prize is to be sent to the winner. Repetition and a random drawing are not proof of a false outcome.

citations.quote: $50 Ulta Gift card Giveaway! (Closed)
Disclaimer: I purchased this myself & all opinions are my own
since i will be needing your address to send it to you
The winner will be selected randomly by random.com or whatever it is

opening.argument: Although presented as a friendly beauty-channel announcement, the video's practical function is promotional: it uses a $50 Ulta gift card to steer viewers into subscribing to two channels, liking a Facebook page, and commenting. The description explicitly calls these rules, and the speaker emphasizes that the giveaway is for subscribers. The beauty context explains why Ulta was chosen, but it does not change the mechanism: an apparently free reward is used to drive audience growth and cross-platform participation. That promotional structure is consistent with a low-barrier reward solicitation, not neutral content.

citations.quote: my channel is a beauty channel so I kind of wanted it to be like to buy beauty stuff
Rules!!!: 1. Must be a subscriber for this channel 2. Must be a subscriber for my vblog channel (link above) 3. Must like my facebook page
I want this video to be for my subscribers because obviously I appreciate you all
be subscriber of this channel and my Other channel

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense describes the content as an ordinary giveaway, but that is precisely the promotional role at issue. The reward is not offered independently of the audience-building conditions: the speaker says it is for subscribers and the written rules require participation across multiple properties. Calling those actions customary does not negate that the video uses a valuable promised item to redirect viewers and expand the creator's audience.

citations.quote: I want this video to be for my subscribers
Must be a subscriber for my vblog channel

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The promotional function is not disputed, but promotion alone is not proof of a scam. The content openly states the entry rules, identifies the prize as a gift card, asks for a comment, and describes selection as random. These quotes show transparent participation terms; they do not show impersonation, payment extraction, fabricated winnings, or a deceptive result.
